title: A Congressman's Plane Lost Power — So He Swam to Safety in a Wisconsin Lake
summary:
What would you do if your plane suddenly lost power over a lake at night? On Saturday, U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany had to find out.

Tiffany, a Republican from Wisconsin, was flying home from a dinner event. He was in a small, single-engine plane — a Beechcraft Bonanza, which seats four people. As the plane approached Wausau Downtown Airport, the engine lost power. The pilot, Leonard Boltz, made an emergency landing right in Lake Wausau.

"After landing, we called 911," Tiffany wrote on X. "As the plane began to submerge, we exited the aircraft and swam to a shallow area, where we waited until emergency responders reached us by boat."

The sheriff's office said it happened just before 9 p.m. A fire department airboat — a flat boat that can glide over water and ice — picked the two men up just after 9 p.m. Both were taken to a hospital, treated for minor injuries, and released. Tiffany needed stitches for a cut above his right eye.

The plane stayed in the lake. A no-wake buoy was placed near it, and boaters were asked to stay away until it can be removed. The Federal Aviation Administration will investigate what went wrong.

Tiffany is running for governor of Wisconsin and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump. His Democratic opponent, David Crowley, wished him a "quick recovery" and praised "the heroism of the pilot."
why_it_matters: It reminds us that pilots train for emergencies and that calling 911 and staying calm — like Tiffany and Boltz did — can matter as much as luck.

background_read: Wisconsin (a state in the northern United States with thousands of lakes and rivers) is a place where small planes and boats are often used to get around. Wausau is a city in that state.
The Federal Aviation Administration, or FAA, is the U.S. government group that makes rules for airplanes and investigates crashes and engine failures.

A U.S. representative (often called a congressman) is elected to help make laws for the whole country; Tom Tiffany represents part of Wisconsin and is now running for governor against David Crowley, with an endorsement from President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025).
Article_Structure: WHO: U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Republican from Wisconsin, and the pilot, Leonard Boltz.
WHAT: Their small single-engine Beechcraft Bonanza lost engine power and made an emergency landing in Lake Wausau; the two men swam to shallow water and were rescued by a fire department airboat.
WHERE: Lake Wausau, near Wausau Downtown Airport in Wisconsin, just before 9 p.m. on Saturday.
WHY: The engine lost power; both men were treated for minor injuries, Tiffany needed stitches above his right eye, and the FAA will investigate the cause.

perspectives.description: They are glad both men survived, and Tiffany's Democratic opponent David Crowley even praised 'the heroism of the pilot.'
They ask why a small plane lost power over water at night, and whether small aircraft are safe enough for regular travel.
They notice the story mixes a frightening accident with a political campaign, since Tiffany is running for governor while people are wishing him well.
